name: Breadcrumbs
summary: Use breadcrumbs to help users understand and move between levels in a website with a deep hierarchy.
whenToUse: Use when a site has multiple hierarchical levels and users need to understand or traverse that structure.
Use the collapse-on-mobile variant for a long path after confirming that the first and final visible items remain useful.
whenNotToUse: Do not use on a site with a flat information architecture.
Do not use breadcrumbs to show progress through a linear transaction.
Never show breadcrumbs together with a back link.

anatomy.name: Navigation landmark
anatomy.description: A nav element has a concise aria-label that identifies the breadcrumb navigation.

anatomy.name: Ordered path
anatomy.description: An ordered list represents the hierarchy from the home page to the current page's parent.

anatomy.name: Breadcrumb links
anatomy.description: Each item links to its corresponding ancestor level.

variants.name: Default
variants.use: A short hierarchy on the standard page background.

variants.name: Collapse on mobile
variants.use: A long path that should show only its first and last items on smaller screens.

variants.name: Inverse
variants.use: A dark background with verified contrast.

behaviour: Place breadcrumbs before main so the page skip link bypasses them.
Start at the site's home page and end at the parent of the current page; do not include the current page as a redundant final link.
The component requires no JavaScript and every link must have a usable href.
accessibility: Use a nav landmark with aria-label="Breadcrumb" or an equivalent localised label.
Retain the ordered-list structure and meaningful link text.
Verify inverse links and separators meet contrast requirements.
content: Use the page or section name for each item and keep it concise.
Ensure adjacent items are distinguishable when announced as a list of links.
